assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's single curated item, reviewed-dedicated-analysis: the canonical V2 character reconstruction model MHA_SP2_KIRISHIMA_EIJIRO_CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL.md at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the Japanese main manga V01-V42 with the source-labeled Ultra Archive, Ultra Analysis and Ultra Age claims its KE-SUP-01 to KE-SUP-03 sections admit. The MHA character modeling schema was consulted for method only; the readiness index, supplemental reconciliation ledger and audit and the deep readings are not curated evidence on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. The model's strong label and its retrospective holdout probe are inputs, not conclusions. No original manga page, anime adaptation, V1 material or other character's model is included, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Kirishima from the V06:p017-018 admiration of Crimson Riot and the V16:p132-148 middle-school freeze and reinvention, through the V10:p062-063 and p082 and V11:p024-025 and p176-177 Bakugo rescue, the V15:p085-117 and V16:p103-123 and p149-151 internship protection under Fat Gum, the V29:p073-085 delivery of the dose to Machia beside Mina, and the V34:p163-168, V36:p039-056 and V38:p133-149 responses to Aoyama, Shoto and Mina, to the V42:p157 adult consideration of hiring. Kept as separable states: frightened middle-schooler, deliberately reinvented student, protective intern, reciprocal war teammate and adult employer; the V16 disclosure is reader-time, not unavailable to his V10 memory, but a V10 freeze cannot use it. No atom covers V01-V05, V07-V09, V12-V14, V17-V28, V30-V33, V35, V37 or V39-V41.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The model states a recurring hierarchy (protect someone within reach, live up to an adopted courageous identity, sustain reciprocal bonds, improve the needed capability), an ideal of a dependable protective person and a feared self who sees the right action and freezes, grounded in located atoms KE01-KE05; the probe KE-V01 rates motive supported. Not B: one compact artifact, one retrospective nonblind probe, and adult private breadth and unsampled moral conflicts are OPEN. Not D: the model is operational, framed as a competition between regret, fear, feasible intervention and responsibility.

Located transitions separate the frightened middle-schooler and the reinvention (KE01), the protective intern who re-hardens after breaking (KE03), the reciprocal war teammate (KE04-KE05) and the adult employer who applies Fat Gum's warning (KE06); the model REVISEs innate fearlessness and simple debt repayment, and KE-SUP-02 separates school concealment from later willing disclosure. Not B: long intervals are unsampled and the adult state rests on one page plus supplements. Not D: change is located, with the epistemic difference between reader disclosure and his own memory stated.

The model identifies 俺, contractions, direct thanks, forceful self-exhortation and 男 and 漢気 vocabulary in peer and field speech, technique naming as performed identity, and the more deliberative register of KE06; it warns against a masculinity slogan in every line, and the probe rates speech/register supported. Not C: no located lines are quoted and private register is little sampled. Not E: a recurrent register and its functional variants are identified and tested on one axis. The discovery row does not enroll SPEECH.

Ordinary conduct in the evidence set is supplement material: daily color shampoo maintaining the school appearance and later casual disclosure of the reinvention (KE-SUP-02, profile fact and author comment) and the girls' framed ranking of his room (KE-SUP-03, a gag). The model says ordinary private conflict is less well sampled than peer and field behavior. Not D: no located enacted ordinary-life routine.

A five-row partner table gives conditional behavior toward Bakugo, Mina, Fat Gum, Class A and Aoyama, and civilians and future employees, with located deltas: Mina from rescuer of his past self to someone he protects (KE01, KE04, KE05), Fat Gum from praise and an enabling role to an employer's responsibility (KE03, KE06), Bakugo's equality-compatible hand (KE02). The probe rates relationship handling supported. Not B: adult and private relations are thinly sampled. Not D: several partners have located, conditioned deltas.

Located interior states are the remembered freeze and the shame of failing to move (KE01, KE02), self-reproach intensified by memory under stress, and admiration turned into obligation (KE05). The probe rates emotional trajectory partial, noting not every internal transition is narrated. Not C: regulation is described in general terms and his interior is inferred mainly from conduct and exhortation. Not E: several located reflective windows exist.

The decision policy is explicit: identify whom intervention serves, assess a workable route, commit to the protective role, persist or re-enter after bodily disruption, and accept help without treating the relation as settled debt; fear may delay it, and courage does not forecast success, endurance or tactical creativity. Located repeatedly in KE02-KE05; the probe rates action supported conditionally. Not B: one probe and a narrow, combat-and-rescue sample; ordinary private conflict is little sampled. Not D: the policy is explicit, repeated and located.

Located choices weigh competing considerations: the Bakugo rescue plan that separates rescue from combat under action pressure (KE02), accepting a coerced Aoyama in view of hidden coercion and pain while the model refuses to generalize to uncoerced betrayal (KE05), and weighing hiring after independence against responsibility for another person's life (KE06, directly checked). Not B: reasoning is mostly inferred from choices and statements, and the adult hypothetical is only medium confidence. Not D: located choices with named competing considerations. The discovery row does not enroll ETHICS.

The model analyzes no humor practice: exuberance and technique naming are described as performed identity, and the room ranking (KE-SUP-03) is others' gag opinion, not his enacted play. This gap says nothing about the character.

The project's analytical corpus is complete for V01-V42 and the admitted supplements; six atoms span V06-V42 with page locators, and the V38 and V42 pages were directly checked. Long intervals are unsampled, the adult state is one page, and the supplements are other-character judgment, editorial summaries, profile facts, an author comment and a gag.

Affirmative limits are located: the model REJECTs invulnerability (Unbreakable can be broken, KE03), REVISEs innate fearlessness and simple debt accounting (KE01, KE05), says no romance with Mina is established by these actions alone, refuses to generalize Aoyama's acceptance to uncoerced repeated betrayal, rejects reading his early phrase as a universal exclusionary law, treats Aizawa's impression of few worries as an observer limit (KE-SUP-01), and says he cannot know a stranger's hidden trauma. Not B: limits rest on few windows in one artifact.

Atoms are page-located with the V31 page convention stated, the V38 and V42 pages are directly checked, the frozen probe separates V16 inputs from V29 comparison and refuses to treat V38's explicit debt rejection as already in the freeze, and the model distinguishes his memory from reader disclosure. Not B: long intervals are unsampled and in-world dates are not given.

scenario_readiness.note: The model quotes no located lines and states that generated dialogue would be an illustrative prediction, never an attributed quotation; register markers are named but private register is little sampled. Lines beyond the described register would be fluent invention. This bounds the evidence set, not Kirishima's actual speech.

conditions: Chronology is one named state, stated explicitly: frightened middle-schooler, reinvented student, protective intern, reciprocal war teammate, or adult employer at V42; employer responsibility is not given to the student and school-era concealment is not replayed by the adult.
The interlocutor is Bakugo, Mina, Fat Gum, a Class A peer including Aoyama, a civilian, or a future employee, handled as the partner table gives; no invented private or romantic relationship.
Hardening varies in strength, duration and recovery; current injury, timing and what ally action the defensive interval permits are specified, and courage does not guarantee success or endurance.

Output is a behavioral description with alternatives; a distant business decision is left information-dependent rather than given an invented instinctive answer, no quoted dialogue is produced as canon and no readiness is inherited from the strong label.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named state: middle-schooler, reinvented student, intern, war teammate or adult employer, stated explicitly.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Bakugo, Mina, Fat Gum, Class A including Aoyama, civilians or future employees, in the relation the partner table gives for that state.
setting_constraints: School, internship, rescue, wartime hero operation or adult agency responsibility
Quirk embodiment, injury and knowledge limits respected
No adult private, leisure or romantic setting

scenario_readiness.note: The model's stated hypothetical (adult Kirishima offered rapid agency expansion with poorly supported junior staff: concern about responsibility and workable support over prestige acceptance, medium confidence from KE06; a sudden rescue emergency prioritizes immediate protection) and the probe's conditionally supported reciprocal courage support narrow novel scenes. The probe is retrospective, nonblind and partial on emotional trajectory.

No enacted ordinary social routine is located; grooming, casual disclosure and the room ranking are supplement profile facts, an author comment and a gag, and the model marks extensive independent adult and private interaction thin.

conditions: The dilemma concerns protection of someone within reach, a coerced or hidden-pain wrongdoer within his class, or responsibility for people he would employ or lead, with the state named.
Output keeps admiration as obligation rather than status envy, refuses debt accounting, and does not generalize acceptance to uncoerced repeated betrayal.
Unsampled moral conflicts and adult private dilemmas are not predicted; the model marks them OPEN.
scenario_readiness.note: Located choices (KE02 rescue versus combat, KE05 coercion-informed acceptance of Aoyama, KE06 responsibility for employees, directly checked) and the model's medium-confidence employer hypothetical support bounded dilemmas only.

The evidence set establishes neither romantic conduct nor its absence; the model says no romance with Mina is established by these actions alone. That limits inference; it says nothing about the character.

conditions: The setting is an internship, a supervised or coordinated hero operation, or an adult employer's decision about staff, with the state stated.
Output preserves fear-compatible protective commitment, hardening limits, acceptance of an enabling role beside a partner, and responsibility for others' lives once he employs them.
Detailed adult agency management, casework and career decisions beyond KE06 are not predicted.
scenario_readiness.note: Professional conduct is located in the internship under Fat Gum (KE03), the war operation (KE04-KE05) and the adult consideration of hiring (KE06, directly checked).

known_limits.statement: Courage is an acquired policy applied under fear, not an absence of fear; the model REVISEs innate fearlessness (KE01).
Unbreakable can be broken and repeated re-hardening costs pain and effort; invulnerability is REJECTed (KE03).
He rejects simple debt accounting with Mina; receiving and giving rescue do not cancel one another (KE04-KE05).
His acceptance of Aoyama is informed by coercion and hidden pain and does not establish acceptance of uncoerced repeated betrayal (KE05).

The manliness vocabulary is his aspirational idiom; the cited interview prevents reducing courage to biological sex, and it is not to be enforced as a universal exclusionary law or inserted in every line.
He does not know a stranger's hidden trauma from recognizing fear; Aizawa's early impression of few worries is an observer limit, not a contradiction of his fear history (KE-SUP-01).
School concealment of his reinvention and later willing public explanation are distinct states; an adult is not given the school-era reaction (KE-SUP-02).
Supplement profile facts, editorial summaries, the author comment and the room-ranking gag (KE-SUP-01 to KE-SUP-03) constrain reconstruction without becoming enacted manga observations.

The single formal probe KE-V01 is a retrospective chronological evidence holdout by an analyst who had read later manga, not a blind experiment; emotional trajectory was partial and the maneuver was unpredicted.
Adult private breadth and unsampled moral conflicts are OPEN in the model; extensive independent adult and private interaction remains thin.
No atom covers V01-V05, V07-V09, V12-V14, V17-V28, V30-V33, V35, V37 or V39-V41, so behavior over those intervals is not established by this evidence set.

The deep readings, readiness index, supplemental reconciliation ledger and audit linked from the model are not curated evidence on this subject, so their warrants were not independently rechecked here. Anime performance and any supplement material beyond what the model cites lie outside this evidence set. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
